ops.d: List every vaults in the subscription.
List the vaults in a resource group.

features.t: Vaults (create, get, list, delete) over ARM
Access configuration (RBAC vs vault access policy, resource access flags)
x: ENFORCED: Vyomi models the one thing the product was missing to make this real — a single simulated signed-in identity (core/azure_arm_core.py CALLER_PRINCIPAL_ID) every Keys/Secrets/Certificates call (tagged with its vault via x-vyomi-vault, the same signal azure.keyvaults.networking enforces against) is evaluated against. The permission-model radio really switches which store is checked: RBAC mode checks a real role assignment covering the vault (or an ancestor resource-group/subscription scope) whose role grants the matching Key Vault dataAction (core/azure_arm_data.py's 'Key Vault *' built-in roles — Administrator/Reader/Secrets Officer/Secrets User/Crypto Officer/Crypto User/Certificates Officer — a SEPARATE dataActions namespace from Owner/Contributor/Reader's actions, matching real Azure: being Owner does not, by itself, grant Key Vault data access once RBAC is on); Vault access policy mode checks the vault's own accessPolicies list (azure.keyvaults.access_policies).

ENFORCED (vault access policy mode only — azure.keyvaults.access_configuration): every Keys/Secrets/Certificates call checks the vault's own accessPolicies list for an entry matching the console's one simulated signed-in principal (CALLER_PRINCIPAL_ID), with the Get/List/Create/Delete bucket the entry's Key/Secret/Certificate Permissions checkboxes already show — Create covers set/update/import too (Vyomi's console exposes those four buckets, not real Key Vault's full per-operation permission set), and a cryptographic operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign/verify/wrap/unwrap) needs at least Get on keys.

Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), and Check access / My access run the real wildcard + scope-inheritance + notActions + explicit-deny decision — all ENFORCED scoped to this vault (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view); Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure. 'Check access' decides a management action (Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write by default) the same way every other resource's IAM blade does; 'My access' is a genuine upgrade over that pattern — since Vyomi has exactly one simulated signed-in principal, it shows THAT principal's real data-plane grant on this vault directly (the RBAC role or access-policy entry azure.keyvaults.access_configuration enforces), not a 'type a principal id' probe.

features.t: Networking (public network access / firewall default action)
x: ENFORCED: the console tags every Keys/Secrets/Certificates call with the vault it's showing (x-vyomi-vault), and publicNetworkAccess:'Disabled' or networkAcls.defaultAction:'Deny' really makes the Key Vault Keys/Secrets/Certificates REST data planes return 403 for that vault (core/azure_arm_core.py keyvault_network_denied, read by core/aws_wire_router.py and core/wire_ingress.py on both substrates).

features.t: Keys (create, get, list, delete) over the Key Vault Keys REST API

x: The RSA public numbers (n/e) advertised on a key are cosmetic (deterministically derived from the private material); the actual cipher behind encrypt/decrypt/wrap/unwrap is a symmetric authenticated envelope, and sign/verify is HMAC-based rather than native RSA/ECDSA. Round-trips (encrypt→decrypt, sign→verify, tamper/cross-key rejection) are real.

features.t: Secrets (set, get, list, list versions, delete) over the Key Vault Secrets REST API
Certificates (generate self-signed, import, get, list, delete) over the Key Vault Certificates REST API
x: Generated (self-signed) certificate creation completes synchronously, and GET .../pending always reports the operation already 'completed' — there is no real multi-step issuance to poll. The `cer`/`x5t` on a GENERATED certificate are deterministic cosmetic bytes, not real X.509 DER.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this vault
x: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this key vault only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a key vault is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the key vault itself.

Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill), and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal. Severity/category filtering is not modelled (every recorded event is Informational/Administrative).

features.t: Key activation/expiration dates, enabled state and tags
x: Activation (nbf), expiration (exp) and disabled state are ENFORCED: encrypt/decrypt/wrap/unwrap/sign/verify on a key outside its window or disabled returns 403 Forbidden.

features.t: Certificate content type, lifetime actions and advanced policy
x: The policy (content type, key size/exportable, lifetime actions) is validated like real Key Vault and stored/returned by Get/UpdateCertificatePolicy, but lifetime actions never fire (no auto-renew or e-mail), and generated certificates are self-signed with placeholder bytes.

Backup returns an opaque integrity-tagged blob containing every version (keys include their material) that restores into any vault of this simulator; a restore over an existing key/secret is a 409 Conflict. Certificate backup/restore and the soft-deleted-object recovery flow are not part of this entry.
